question.text: This was the largest boat of the three in Columbus's fleet. It ran aground due to incompetent piloting and was dismantled to build the first Spanish settlement in the New World.
question.clue: This ship, the largest and slowest of the three that Christopher Columbus used in his first voyage to the Americas.

swap.text: Conquistadors from this European nation conquered the Incas. This empire established colonies in all of Central America and most of South America.
swap.clue: Emilio Mola's troops in this country were opposed by the Connolly Column and the Abraham Lincoln Brigade, both part of the International Brigades that fought here.

question.leadin: In 1099, Valencian soldiers scared away Almoravid invaders by placing this leader's body on his horse Bavieca, making it appear he had returned from the dead.
question.text: Name this legendary Spanish warrior, a mercenary who fought on behalf of the Emir of Zaragoza against King Alfonso XI of Castile before claiming Valencia as his own.
question.answerHtml: El Cid [or Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar; prompt on Díaz alone; or El Campeador or the Champion, or Le Cid]
question.clue: This ruler of Valencia who fought both for and against the Taifa of Zargoza.

swap.text: The Umayyad Caliphate would later be expelled by the Abbasids, but it maintained its rule on this peninsula. Christians on this peninsula would later lead a campaign against the Muslims called the Reconquista.
swap.clue: The knight El Cid fought on both sides of a series of military campaigns in this region, which concluded in 1492 with the fall of the Emirate of Granada.

question.text: Franco was a member of this Fascist party founded by Jose Antonio Primo de Rivera. Under his oversight, it merged with the monarchist Carlists.
question.answerHtml: Falange [accept Spanish Phalanx of the Assemblies of the National Syndicalist Offensive; accept Falangists]
question.clue: Two leaders of this party were buried within the Santa Cruz Basilica at the Valley of the Fallen.

swap.leadin: This war was supposed to be avoided through the First and Second Partition Treaties.
swap.text: Name this 13-year conflict over control of an Iberian nation. It was sparked by the death of the childless King Charles II.
swap.clue: The collapse of the Grand Alliance was prevented after the Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy won this war's Battle of Blenheim, and the North American theater of this war was Queen Anne's War.

question.leadin: The County of Barcelona and this kingdom were once ruled by a monarchy called its namesake "Crown."
question.text: Name this kingdom whose monarchs included Joanna the Mad and Henry VIII's first wife Catherine.
question.clue: A princess of this kingdom was the first woman named as an ambassador to another European nation, in this case England.

swap.leadin: Prior to the defeat of this force, one monarch claimed that she had "the heart and stomach of a king."
swap.text: Name this invading military force which was hindered by the "Protestant wind" and defeated at the Battle of Gravelines ["gravf-leen"].
swap.answerHtml: The Spanish Armada (or Grande y Felicísima Armada; prompt on “Spanish navy” and equivalents)
swap.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

question.text: The successor to Pedro Gonzales de Mendoza as the Archbishop of Toledo, this advisor to Isabella was eventually promoted to Grand Inquisitor after he brokered the Agreement of Salamanca, ending a potential succession crisis involving Philip I of Castile. In his later years he led a crusade against the Muslim held city of Oran.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the Sale Corsairs.
swap.text: The Sale Corsairs were based out of New Sale, a city founded after Philip III expelled these people from Spain in 1610. This Spanish term refers to the Muslims who stayed in Spain after the reconquest and converted to Christianity.
swap.answerHtml: Moriscos [do not accept terms like "Moors" or "Muslims" that are not Spanish]
swap.clue: This silk trade-controlling group created the maritime Republic of Sale (SAL-ay), and unsuccessfully sought aid from the Huguenot stronghold of Bearn.

question.leadin: This city is home to the world's oldest functioning lighthouse, the Tower of Hercules, and was referred to as The Groyne in some archaic English contexts.
question.text: Name this city in northwestern Spain, home to the Royal Galician Academy.

swap.text: The first of the Spanish Bourbons was this grandson of Louis XIV. His accession in 1700 prompted the War of Spanish Succession, though he would stay in power until his death in 1746.
swap.clue: This king's opponents claimed that his reign was a violation of the Hague Partition Treaties.

question.text: In modern times, this Spanish General put down a Syndicalist revolt in Asturias in the lead up to the Spanish Civil War. This dictator defeated the Republican forces of Manuel Azana in that civil war and ruled Spain for forty years.
question.clue: In another conflict, this future leader worked with a commander who coined the phrase "fifth column" and was aided by the Condor Legion.

swap.leadin: This autonomous community contains the provinces of Malaga and Cadiz.
swap.text: Name this southernmost autonomous community of Spain that contains the city of Granada.
swap.clue: This region is also home to the city of Cadiz, which, owing to its strategic position, was raided by Sir Francis Drake seeking to impede the Spanish Armada and blockaded by Lord Nelson before the Battle of Trafalgar.

question.leadin: The Duke of Wellington created the lines of Torres Vedras to protect one capital in this conflict, which was triggered by an 1807 invasion led by Jean-Andoche Junot.
question.text: Name this conflict in which Napoleon's forces invaded Spain and Portugal.
question.clue: One general in this war was made Duke of Ciudad Rodrigo by the Spanish Government, and was also given a dukedom in Britain.

swap.leadin: This campaign was legendarily brought on after a king opened 27 padlocks to enter a chamber and read a scroll, which prophesied that the horsemen painted on the walls would invade his kingdom.
swap.text: Describe this campaign that began with the defeat of King Roderic at an early 8th-century AD battle that was won by a Berber general.
swap.answerHtml: the Arab conquest of Spain [accept answers with Umayyad or Muslim or Tariq ibn Ziyad in place of “Arab”; accept the fall of the Visigothic Kingdom or clear equivalents; accept answers with synonyms for conquest or fall; accept the Battle of Guadalete or the Battle of 711; accept answers with Iberia or Hispania or Andalusia or al-Andalus or the Visigothic Kingdom in place of “Spain”]

question.text: This conservative Spanish prime minister switched places with Liberal Praxedes Mateo Sagasta during the turno pacifico. His support of the Carlists led to his 1897 assassination by Italian anarchist Michel Angiolillo.

swap.text: After the war, Philip V issued this set of laws that removed the autonomy of regions that were formerly part of the Aragonese crown, including abolishing the traditional charters of Valencia and Catalonia, in an attempt to create a centralized Spanish state.
swap.clue: Carlism gained major support from Basque and Catalan communities by promising to reverse these laws of Philip V, which revoked the autonomy of Spain's peripheral communities.

question.leadin: Spain had a famous some Restoration periods too. Answer the following about one of them, FTPE.
question.text: After the brief experiment of the First Republic, this Bourbon son of Isabella II was given the throne in 1874, establishing a constitutional monarchy in its place.
question.clue: This man, who spent part of his time in exile attending Sandhurst College, returned to Spain and was proclaimed king following the overthrow of the First Spanish Republic. Antonio Canovas de Castillo promulgated the royalist constitution during this monarch's reign in 1876.

swap.leadin: This dynasty featured five rulers named Yusuf and thirteen rulers named Muhammed.
swap.text: Name this dynasty whose final two members included one dubbed "El Zagal," who was captured and imprisoned in Tunis, and one dubbed "Boabdil," who surrendered its capital city to two monarchs.
